She rose to international fame for her role as [Phoebe Buffay](/wiki/Phoebe_Buffay "Phoebe Buffay") in the American television sitcom *[Friends](/wiki/Friends "Friends")*, which aired from 1994 to 2004. The series earned her [Primetime Emmy](/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Awards "Primetime Emmy Awards"), [Screen Actors Guild](/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Awards "Screen Actors Guild Awards"), [Satellite](/wiki/Satellite_Awards "Satellite Awards"), [American Comedy](/wiki/American_Comedy_Awards "American Comedy Awards") and [TV Guide](/wiki/TV_Guide_Award "TV Guide Award") awards. Phoebe has since been named one of the greatest television characters of all time and is considered to be Kudrow's breakout role, spawning her successful film career.

Kudrow initially appeared in a 1989 episode of the hit sitcom *[Cheers](/wiki/Cheers "Cheers")* playing a character named Emily. [Mariah Carey](/wiki/Mariah_Carey "Mariah Carey") topped the chart with her song "[We Belong Together](/wiki/We_Belong_Together "We Belong Together")". She also reached No. 15 with "[Shake It Off](/wiki/Shake_It_Off_(Mariah_Carey_song) "Shake It Off (Mariah Carey song)")" and No. 69 with "[It's Like That](/wiki/It%27s_Like_That_(Mariah_Carey_song) "It's Like That (Mariah Carey song)")" featuring [Jermaine Dupri](/wiki/Jermaine_Dupri "Jermaine Dupri") and [Fatman Scoop](/wiki/Fatman_Scoop "Fatman Scoop").

The [*Billboard* Hot 100](/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") is a chart that ranks the best-performing [singles](/wiki/Single_(music) "Single (music)") in the United States. Its data, published by *[Billboard](/wiki/Billboard_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")* magazine and compiled by [Nielsen SoundScan](/wiki/Nielsen_SoundScan "Nielsen SoundScan"), is based collectively on each single's weekly [physical](/wiki/CD_single "CD single") and [digital](/wiki/Digital_distribution "Digital distribution") sales, as well as [airplay](/wiki/Heavy_rotation "Heavy rotation") and [streaming](/wiki/Streaming_media "Streaming media"). At the end of a year, *Billboard* will publish an annual list of the 100 most successful songs throughout that year on the Hot 100 chart based on the information. For 2005, the list was published on December 20, calculated with data from December 4, 2004, to November 26, 2005.[[1]](#cite_note-1) The R&B track "[We Belong Together](/wiki/We_Belong_Together "We Belong Together")" by American singer [Mariah Carey](/wiki/Mariah_Carey "Mariah Carey") was named the number 1 song of 2005, and it spent the longest time at number 1 for the year, 14 weeks. fanoutqa_001420.t: Alaska :: History :: Good Friday earthquake :: part 01 :: chunk_0009
fanoutqa_001420.x:
Alaska :: History :: Good Friday earthquake :: part 01 :: chunk_0009
Main article: [1964 Alaska earthquake](/wiki/1964_Alaska_earthquake "1964 Alaska earthquake")

On March 27, 1964, the massive [Good Friday earthquake](/wiki/1964_Alaska_earthquake "1964 Alaska earthquake") killed 133 people and destroyed several villages and portions of large coastal communities, mainly by the resultant [tsunamis](/wiki/Tsunamis "Tsunamis") and landslides. It was the [fourth-most-powerful earthquake](/wiki/Largest_earthquakes_by_magnitude "Largest earthquakes by magnitude") in recorded history, with a [moment magnitude](/wiki/Moment_magnitude_scale "Moment magnitude scale") of 9.2 (more than a thousand times as powerful as the [1989 San Francisco earthquake](/wiki/1989_Loma_Prieta_earthquake "1989 Loma Prieta earthquake")).[[28]](#cite_note-30) The time of day (5:36 pm), time of year (spring) and location of the [epicenter](/wiki/Epicenter "Epicenter") were all cited as factors in potentially sparing thousands of lives, particularly in Anchorage.

The Good Friday earthquake lasted 4 minutes and 38 seconds. Six hundred miles (970 km) of fault ruptured at once and moved up to 60 ft (18 m), releasing about 500 years of stress buildup. [Soil liquefaction](/wiki/Soil_liquefaction "Soil liquefaction"), fissures, landslides, and other ground failures caused major structural damage in several communities and much damage to property. [Anchorage](/wiki/Anchorage,_Alaska "Anchorage, Alaska") sustained great destruction or damage to many inadequately [earthquake-engineered](/wiki/Earthquake_engineering "Earthquake engineering") houses, buildings, and infrastructure (paved streets, sidewalks, water and sewer mains, electrical systems, and other human-made equipment), particularly in the several landslide zones along [Knik Arm](/wiki/Knik_Arm "Knik Arm"). Two hundred miles (320 km) southwest, some areas near [Kodiak](/wiki/Kodiak_Island "Kodiak Island") were permanently raised by 30 feet (9 m).

Box office analysts, on the other hand, estimated that the film would be a success.[[217]](#cite_note-Slate-241)[[222]](#cite_note-MTV-247) Some believed its use of 3D would help its box office performance, given that recent 3D films had been successful.[[217]](#cite_note-Slate-241) "The holy grail of 3D has finally arrived," wrote an analyst for Exhibitor Relations. "This is why all these 3D venues were built: for *Avatar.* This is the one. The behemoth."[[222]](#cite_note-MTV-247) One "cautionary estimate" was that *Avatar* would bring in around $60 million during its opening weekend, although other estimates were higher.[[222]](#cite_note-MTV-247)[[223]](#cite_note-Hollywood_Elsewhere-248)
